LifestyleQuestionnaire.title: Costa Rica Lifestyle Discovery Questionnaire
LifestyleQuestionnaire.tagline: Tell Me How You Want to Live, and I'll Tell You Where to Find It

welcome.heading: Welcome to the Southern Zone & Valley Region!
welcome.description: Finding your perfect home here isn't just about bedrooms or square footage—it’s about matching your daily rhythm to the right microclimate, road infrastructure, and community vibe.
welcome.timeEstimate: Take 3 minutes to fill out this lifestyle check, and we will pinpoint the exact local neighborhood that matches your vision.

LifestyleQuestionnaire.question: Question

q1.title: 1. The Morning Rhythm & Climate
q1.subtitle: When you wake up and look out the window, what do you want to see and feel?
q1.a: High-energy vibe. I want to feel the tropical heat and enjoy a vibrant, sun-drenched environment.
q1.b: Immersed in nature. I want elevated, sweeping views, lush green surroundings, and a continuous breeze.
q1.c: Fresh and tranquil. I prefer cool breezes, rolling green hills, and a milder climate where I can avoid using A/C.

q2.title: 2. Driving, Access & Road Realities
q2.subtitle: How do you honestly feel about unpaved roads and rugged terrain?
q2.a: All paved, flat, and easy roads. I prefer highly accessible streets where any standard vehicle can go.
q2.b: I can handle some adventure, but within limits. Solid gravel or well-maintained community roads are fine.
q2.c: Bring on the adventure! Fully comfortable with rugged 4x4 tracks to get ultimate privacy and pristine nature.

q3.title: 3. Convenience, Errands & Healthcare
q3.subtitle: How far are you willing to drive for major supermarkets, banking, and medical care?
q3.a: Boutique convenience right down the street. Walk or 5-minute drive to organic markets, pharmacies, and local eateries.
q3.b: Quiet seclusion. I don't mind a 15- to 20-minute scenic drive to get my errands done.
q3.c: Full municipal city convenience. I want immediate access to regional hospitals, corporate banks, and major supermarkets.

q4.title: 4. Community Vibe & Social Circles
q4.subtitle: What does your ideal neighbor network and social scene look like?
q4.a: Bohemian and fluid blend of world-class surfers, digital nomads, eco-travelers, and active evening social scenes.
q4.b: International, wellness-oriented expat community tightly integrated with local Tico culture (farmers' markets, yoga).
q4.c: Authentic, relationship-driven Costa Rican lifestyle. Sprawling country estates, local farmers, and homesteaders.

a.title: The Coastal Surf & High-Energy Hub
a.vibe: You want immediate beach energy, a walkable or easy-drive lifestyle, and a lively social connection. You don't want to be isolated on a high mountain ridge; you want to be where the action is.

p1.name: Dominical
p1.desc: The ultimate capital for world-class surf, bohemian nightlife, and digital nomad energy. Mostly flat, highly walkable town center with paved access right off the Costanera.

p2.name: Dominicalito
p2.desc: Just south of Dominical. It offers a slightly quieter, gentler cove beach vibe, highly favored by long-term residents who want easy 2WD ocean proximity without the high tourist traffic of main Dominical.

p3.name: Bahía Ballena
p3.desc: Nestled right against the Marino Ballena National Park. Flat, easy to drive, highly bikeable, and perfect for buyers who want to walk into the national park every morning to see the pristine shoreline.

b.title: The Coastal Jungle Ridge & Eco-Luxury Lifestyle
b.vibe: You want the dramatic "wow factor"—where the lush jungle canopy directly overlooks the Pacific Ocean. You prioritize sweeping views, wildlife, and premium alternative learning/wellness communities, and you don't mind a 4x4 mountain road to get to your private sanctuary.

p1.name: Uvita
p1.desc: The undisputed center of gravity for services on the coast. Home to diverse restaurants, supermarkets, pharmacies, and thriving bilingual and alternative learning communities. The lower parts are flat and easy; the ridges require a solid 4x4 but offer spectacular views of the Whale's Tail.

p2.name: Platanillo
p2.desc: Perched on the paved ridge road halfway between the coast and the inland valley. It sits at a higher elevation, offering cooler temperatures, lush mountain rainforest views, rushing waterfalls, and a strong, tight-knit community of eco-conscious expats and locals just 15 minutes from the beach.

p3.name: Barú
p3.desc: A pristine, nature-first river valley and mountain zone stretching inland along the Barú River. Ideal for those who want massive biodiversity, privacy, and close proximity to nature reserves while keeping the beach within a short, scenic drive.

c.title: The Authentic Mountain Valley & High-Convenience Lifestyle
c.vibe: You want maximum value, spacious acreage, an authentic connection to Costa Rican culture, and zero reliance on 24/7 air conditioning. You prioritize robust, city-level infrastructure over immediate beach access.

p1.name: Pérez Zeledón (including San Isidro de El General)
p1.desc: The major economic and agricultural powerhouse of the region. This is a full-scale municipal city hub offering a top-tier regional hospital, major private medical clinics, corporate banking, massive weekly organic Ferias, and endless commercial conveniences.

p2.name: Surrounding Pérez Areas (e.g., General Viejo, Miravalles, Quebradas, Cajón)
p2.desc: These surrounding mountain foothills offer sprawling country estates, rich soil for planting, cool mountain air, and dramatic vistas of the Talamanca mountain range—all while being a seamless 10- to 15-minute paved drive into downtown San Isidro for errands.

FAQ.metaTitle: Relocating to Costa Rica FAQs | RE/MAX Altitud
FAQ.metaDescription: Find answers to the most common questions about relocating to Costa Rica. Learn about areas, cost of living, property types, and why buying is better than renting.
FAQ.intro: Everything you need to know before making your move to Costa Rica's Southern Zone.
FAQ.q1_question: Is Costa Rica a good place to relocate?
FAQ.q1_answer: Yes, Costa Rica is an exceptional place to relocate. It offers a wide variety of areas with completely different prices, lifestyles, and affordability. Whether you want to wake up to misty mountain views in Pérez Zeledón or enjoy the tropical warmth and world-class surfing along the coast in Dominical and Uvita, there's an area tailored perfectly to your pace and budget.
FAQ.q2_question: Should I rent before buying in Costa Rica?
FAQ.q2_answer: It is not needed to rent. If you do your investigation and scouting trips you do not need to rent before buying. Instead of reading online, have a discovery call... people talk about Costa Rica online as if it were a small city and because they spent 2 months in the north, they think that is the reality of the south too. And you can always sell what you bought if you did not like it.
FAQ.q3_question: Are there places for specific lifestyles (e.g., bohemian, luxury, off-grid)?
FAQ.q3_answer: Absolutely. Costa Rica is culturally and socially diverse. There are specific enclaves for almost every lifestyle: luxury and entrepreneur-oriented communities for networking, bohemian coastal towns perfect for creatives, and places for individuals prioritizing medical freedom and natural health choices (such as those who prefer no vaccines). We can match you with the exact community that shares your values.
FAQ.q4_question: What is the cost of living like in Costa Rica?
FAQ.q4_answer: The cost of living varies wildly depending on your lifestyle and location. Coastal towns like Uvita and Dominical lean toward premium pricing due to high tourist demand, whereas mountain areas like Pérez Zeledón and its surrounding valleys offer a much lower cost of living, abundant local organic produce, and a truly authentic Costa Rican lifestyle.
FAQ.q5_question: Can foreigners buy property in Costa Rica?
FAQ.q5_answer: Yes, foreigners have the exact same property rights as Costa Rican citizens when buying titled land. You do not need a local partner to buy a house or a lot.
FAQ.q6_question: Do I need residency to buy a house?
FAQ.q6_answer: No, you do not need to be a resident to purchase property; you can buy on a standard tourist visa. In fact, purchasing a property valued over a certain threshold can actually qualify you to apply for an Investor Residency.
FAQ.q7_answer: We have trustable builders and the design of the house is free of charge when you buy with us.
FAQ.q8_question: What is the process of buying a property?
FAQ.q8_answer: Once you choose the property, we do a Letter of Intent (LOI) or Sales and Purchase Agreement (SPA). You do a downpayment (which is refundable if the Due Diligence is not what we expected) and then you buy the house.
FAQ.q9_question: Do I buy under my name or a company?
FAQ.q9_answer: We can have a call with our lawyers to see what is best for you and your plans.

FAQ.q11_answer: Yes. Many areas of Costa Rica have schools in English.
FAQ.q12_question: What is the healthcare system like?
FAQ.q12_answer: Costa Rica has a dual, highly regarded healthcare system. There is the public system, known as the Caja (CCSS), which legal residents pay into monthly and can use for free. There is also an excellent private healthcare system with world-class hospitals (mostly centered around the Central Valley) where procedures and private insurance are a fraction of US costs.
FAQ.q13_question: Can I legally work or start a business there?
FAQ.q13_answer: As a general rule, immigrants cannot hold a local job that could otherwise be filled by a Costa Rican citizen. However, you can legally own a business and manage it, work completely online as a remote employee or freelancer for companies outside of Costa Rica, or work legally once you achieve permanent residency (which usually takes a few years of temporary residency).
FAQ.q14_question: Do I absolutely need to speak fluent Spanish?
FAQ.q14_answer: You don't need to be fluent to survive, especially in heavily populated expat hubs or tourist destinations where English is widely spoken. However, to truly integrate, build relationships with your neighbors, navigate government bureaucracy, and show respect to the local culture, putting effort into learning Spanish makes a massive difference in how successful your relocation will be.
FAQ.q15_question: Is Costa Rica safe to live in?
FAQ.q15_answer:
Costa Rica is rightfully famous for its peace, its solid democracy, and the warmth of its people. Traveling or living here is an extremely safe experience. In the city and the busiest tourist areas, the only real challenge is being careless with personal belongings. In contrast, non-tourist areas are oases of tranquility so extreme that it's normal to see neighbors with their house doors open.

Here, true "safety" has more to do with nature and the roads: the main recommendation is to avoid driving at night or under heavy rain, as visibility decreases significantly and, being mountain or rural routes, roadside assistance can take a little longer to arrive. Cautious driving is the key to enjoying the trip!
FAQ.q16_question: How do I bring my pets with me?
FAQ.q16_answer: Bringing domestic pets to Costa Rica is highly doable and does not require a quarantine period. It does, however, require strict coordination with a certified veterinarian to secure specific international health certificates, up-to-date rabies vaccinations, and endorsed paperwork within a tight window before your flight.
FAQ.q17_question: What is the infrastructure really like (Internet, Roads, Utilities)?
FAQ.q17_answer: High-speed fiber optic internet is now widely available across most popular beach and mountain towns, making remote work entirely seamless. That said, depending on how remote you live, you have to be prepared for the occasional power bump or water outage during major storms, and navigating certain rural areas still requires a reliable 4x4 vehicle due to unpaved roads and river crossings.
FAQ.conclusion: The Takeaway: The people who transition most successfully to Costa Rica are the ones who don't try to force their old lifestyle onto their new country. It’s all about trading convenience for quality of life, and speed for peace of mind.
